requirements.evidence: Defaults + range fallback in Queue::defaultPrefixFor (app/Models/Queue.php:71-86) and DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP const; prefixForPriority custom-first (Queue.php:52-69); normalizePriorityPrefixMap validates canonical keys with '/\A(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\z/', single A-Z values, uniqueness incl. default fallbacks for uncovered 0/10/20, [] -> null, enforced in static::saving (Queue.php:30-35). Ticket::nextCode filters whereDate('issue_date', ...) and a prefix pattern '([0-9]{3,})' ordered by id, skipping malformed/legacy codes (Ticket.php:40-63). IssueTicket reads now() once and uses it for code day, issued_at and issue_date (IssueTicket.php:27-28, 60-61). Migration adds nullable, backfills DATE(issued_at), makes NOT NULL, swaps unique index, has down(). Factory aligns issue_date with issued_at and allocates by priority/day while keeping explicit codes. UpdateQueue gains ?array $priorityPrefixMap with null/[]/validate semantics, wraps InvalidArgumentException into ValidationException keyed priority_prefix_map before mutating anything. Docs and CHANGELOG updated.

conventions.evidence: Domain write goes through UpdateQueue with Gate authorize kept first; map excluded from #[Fillable] (Queue.php:13) and IssueTicket uses forceCreate for system fields; migrations carry generator-style timestamps (2026_10_29_055636/055637) with down(); PHPDoc on new public methods; docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG [Unreleased] updated. Small deviations: catch-all InvalidArgumentException around $queue->save() in UpdateQueue and a redundant mutator style differ slightly from the lean sibling style.

security.evidence: priority_prefix_map not mass-assignable (test 'does not mass-assign the priority prefix map'); UpdateQueue authorizes via Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('update', $queue) before validation; strict regex validation of keys/values with \A..\z anchors (rejects trailing newline, tested); issue_date not fillable. No Livewire/Blade surface touched.

tests.evidence: New tests/Feature/QueuePrefixMapTest.php (defaults, range fallback, custom map, empty->null, mass-assignment, 12-case invalid-map dataset incl. {'0':'E'} and duplicates, save-time validation, UpdateQueue set/unchanged/clear, ValidationException leaves queue unchanged, employee denied), TicketFactoryTest.php (priority prefix, custom map, historical day N001, explicit code alignment), TicketSchemaTest.php (column nullability/type, new unique index, cross-day N001), IssueTicketTest updates (independent prefixes, midnight travelTo test, legacy A, malformed skip, N999->N1000). Missing: no test of the migration backfill from DATE(issued_at) or of down().

simplicity.evidence: Mostly lean, but some redundancy: prefixForPriority checks both array_key_exists($priority) and array_key_exists((string) $priority) although PHP coerces numeric-string keys to int (Queue.php:58-64); the first uniqueness loop's '$usedPrefixes[$prefix] !== $priority' is always true since keys are unique; the Ticket issueDate mutator has identical 'is_string' and 'default' match arms (Ticket.php:153-158); UpdateQueue validates the map up front and again catches InvalidArgumentException on save.

readability.evidence: Clear names (normalizePriorityPrefixMap, defaultPrefixFor), explanatory comments on the single clock read and the factory alignment, updated nextCode docblock. The factory afterMaking if/elseif chain for issued_at/issue_date (TicketFactory.php:44-59) is a bit dense but understandable; minor dead branches noted under simplicity.

scope.evidence: All changes serve the task: models, actions, factories, two migrations, required docs, tests. The docs/api/totem.md edit only updates the example/description of the code format to stay in sync, no API behavior change.

issues.explanation: dropUnique(['queue_id','code']) runs before the new index is created as separate statements; on MariaDB this fails if that unique index is the only index backing the queue_id foreign key (cannot be verified from the diff), so adding the new index first would be safer.
The backfill of existing rows from DATE(issued_at) and the down() path have no test coverage.
Catching every InvalidArgumentException from save() and reporting it as a priority_prefix_map error is redundant with the up-front normalization and could mislabel unrelated exceptions.
The string-key lookup in prefixForPriority is dead code because PHP normalizes numeric string keys to ints.
The is_string and default match arms are identical; one arm suffices.
The '!== $priority' guard in the custom-entry uniqueness loop is always true since map keys are unique.

review.summary: The change implements priority-prefixed (N/P/E or per-queue custom) ticket codes with per-day, per-prefix sequences: a validated, non-mass-assignable priority_prefix_map on Queue, an issue_date column with backfill and the new unique index, a single clock read in IssueTicket, a factory aligned to issued_at, an UpdateQueue parameter that raises ValidationException, plus docs and broad tests. All requirements and the contract are covered and the tests are thorough. Remaining points are small: a possible MariaDB foreign-key ordering risk in the index swap, no test for the migration backfill, and a few redundant branches. I would approve with nits.
